method_card.title: The Natural World and Environment
method_card.content:
This lesson covers the natural world, environmental problems, and solutions — using modal verbs for advice and obligation, future tense for predictions, and compound noun decomposition.

GermanEnglish
die Umweltthe environment
die Umweltverschmutzungpollution
der Klimawandelclimate change
der Müll / der Abfallrubbish / waste
recycelnto recycle
die Mülltrennungwaste separation
umweltfreundlichenvironmentally friendly
die erneuerbare Energierenewable energy
man muss / man sollteone must / one should
der Wald (ä-er)forest
der Berg (-e)mountain
die Tierweltwildlife / animal kingdom
das Meer (-e)sea
die Naturnature
(Higher) nachhaltigsustainable

Grammar focus 1 — man muss/sollte + infinitive at end: man (one / you / people in general) takes the er/sie/es verb form. Modal muss (must) or sollte (should) sits at position 2; the main verb goes to the end as an infinitive. Man muss Energie sparen. (One must save energy.) Man sollte weniger Auto fahren. (One should drive less.) This is the most common error: placing the infinitive directly after the modal instead of at the end.

Grammar focus 2 — future tense: werden + infinitive at end: werden conjugates at position 2; the infinitive goes to the end. Der Klimawandel wird schlimmer werden. (Climate change will get worse.) Es wird mehr Überschwemmungen geben. (There will be more floods — note geben at the end.)

Grammar focus 3 — compound nouns: German builds long nouns from parts. The gender of a compound noun = the gender of the last element. die Umweltverschmutzung = Umwelt + Verschmutzung (from die Verschmutzung → feminine). der Klimawandel = Klima + Wandel (from der Wandel → masculine). die Mülltrennung = Müll + Trennung (from die Trennung → feminine). Breaking them down reveals their meaning.

Model: Der Klimawandel ist ein großes Problem. Man sollte weniger Strom verbrauchen und mehr recyceln. Ich fahre mit dem Rad zur Schule, weil es umweltfreundlich ist. Wenn wir nichts tun, wird die Tierwelt leiden. (Climate change is a big problem. One should use less electricity and recycle more. I cycle to school because it is environmentally friendly. If we do nothing, wildlife will suffer.)
steps: Learn environmental and natural world vocabulary including each noun's gender (der/die/das)
Master man muss/sollte + infinitive at the end of the clause — never place the infinitive next to the modal
Practise future tense: werden + infinitive at end
Decompose compound nouns to work out their meaning and gender
Build balanced arguments combining modal verbs, future tense, and weil + verb-final

exam_context.frequency: Popular topic — environment appears in writing, speaking, reading and listening tasks

worked_examples.question: What does 'Umweltverschmutzung' mean? How do you work it out?

steps.label: Combine the parts
steps.content: Environment + pollution = environmental pollution. The gender = gender of the last element: die Verschmutzung → die Umweltverschmutzung.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Environmental pollution. Break down long compound nouns into their parts to work out meaning and gender.

worked_examples.question: Translate: 'One should use public transport.' How does the modal verb work?

steps.label: Modal verb
steps.content: man sollte = one should. sollte is the Konjunktiv II of sollen — it sits at position 2.

steps.label: Infinitive at end
steps.content: The main verb goes to the end as an infinitive: benutzen (to use).

worked_examples.question: Translate the wenn-clause: 'If we do nothing, climate change will get worse.'

steps.label: Identify the subordinate clause
steps.content: wenn (if) introduces a subordinate clause — the conjugated verb goes to the end of that clause: Wenn wir nichts tun.

steps.label: Build the main clause
steps.content: Because the subordinate clause comes first, the main clause has inversion (verb-second): wird at position 2, then subject der Klimawandel, then the rest — with the infinitive werden at the very end: wird der Klimawandel schlimmer werden.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Wenn wir nichts tun, wird der Klimawandel schlimmer werden.

bronze.question: Match the German environmental words to the English meaning
Match the German to the English meaning
Complete the sentence — modal verb + infinitive at end

gaps.correct_explain: sollte = should (Konjunktiv II of sollen). Man sollte = one should. muss (must) is also correct — it expresses stronger obligation.

wrong.kann: kann means 'can'. The sentence expresses advice ('should'), so use sollte.
wrong.soll: soll means 'is supposed to'. sollte (Konjunktiv II) expresses gentle advice.

gaps.rule: Infinitive at end with modal verb
gaps.correct_explain: fahren is the infinitive, placed at the end of the clause. Modal verbs send the second verb to the end.

wrong.fährt: fährt is a conjugated form. After a modal verb, use the infinitive: fahren.

gaps.correct_explain: Rad (bicycle) — mit dem Rad fahren = to cycle. Fahrrad also accepted.

wrong.Auto: Auto is a car, which is not environmentally friendly. The sentence says umweltfreundlich.

gaps.rule: Predicative adjective — no ending after ist
gaps.correct_explain: umweltfreundlich = environmentally friendly. After ist (predicative position), adjectives take no ending.

bronze.question: What does 'Jeder kann etwas für die Umwelt tun' mean?
options: Everyone can do something for the environment
Something should be done about pollution

bronze.question: What does 'Es wird mehr Überschwemmungen geben' mean?

bronze.source_text: Ich recycele Papier, Glas und Plastik. Ich benutze keine Plastiktüten.
model_answers: I recycle paper, glass and plastic. I don't use plastic bags.
hints: keine = no / not any (negation of noun)

Note: 'keine Plastiktüten' uses kein (not nicht) to negate the noun. Be encouraging. bronze.question: Listen and type what you hear
bronze.audio_text: Man muss Wasser und Energie sparen.
bronze.correct_text: Man muss Wasser und Energie sparen.
bronze.translation: One must save water and energy.

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: Climate change **threatens** our planet. There **will be** more droughts.
sentence_parts: unseren Planeten. Es wird mehr Dürren

gaps.correct_explain: bedroht is the er/sie/es form of bedrohen (to threaten). Der Klimawandel is masculine singular — er-form.

wrong.bedrohen: bedrohen is the infinitive or wir/sie plural form. The subject is singular: use bedroht.

gaps.rule: Future tense — werden + infinitive at end
gaps.correct_explain: geben is the infinitive. With wird (future), the main verb goes to the end: Es wird mehr Dürren geben = there will be more droughts.

wrong.gibt: gibt is the present tense form. With wird (future), use the infinitive: geben.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.explanation: After modal verbs, use the infinitive. The infinitive of 'to use' is benutzen. benutzten is the simple past plural form — wrong here.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: We must separate the rubbish and save energy.

distractor_labels.muss: wrong form — the subject is wir (we), so use müssen not muss (ich/er/sie/es form).

silver.source_text: I shower instead of bathing and I turn the light off when I leave a room.
model_answers: Ich dusche statt zu baden, und ich mache das Licht aus, wenn ich ein Zimmer verlasse.
hints: when I leave = wenn ich verlasse

Check: statt zu + infinitive (zu + infinitive structure), separable verb ausmachen splits in main clause (mache...aus), wenn + verb-final (verlasse at end). Accept valid alternatives e.g. Ich dusche anstatt zu baden. silver.question: Listen and type what you hear
silver.audio_text: Man sollte weniger Auto fahren und mehr recyceln.
silver.correct_text: Man sollte weniger Auto fahren und mehr recyceln.
silver.translation: One should drive less and recycle more.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: If we do nothing, climate change will get worse. There will be more floods and many animals will become extinct. In the future we must use more renewable energy.
model_answers: Wenn wir nichts tun, wird der Klimawandel schlimmer werden. Es wird mehr Überschwemmungen geben und viele Tiere werden aussterben. In Zukunft müssen wir mehr erneuerbare Energie benutzen.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a Gold-tier translation. Source: '{source}'. Model answer: '{model}'. Check: wenn + verb-final (tun at end of wenn-clause), inversion after wenn-clause in main clause (wird der Klimawandel — verb second), future with werden + infinitive at end (werden schlimmer werden, geben, aussterben), separable verb aussterben (prefix stays joined in infinitive form), modal müssen + infinitive at end (benutzen). Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: On the one hand, renewable energy is good for the environment. On the other hand, it is often expensive.

distractor_labels.er: wrong pronoun — Energie is feminine (die Energie), so the pronoun is sie, not er.
distractor_labels.Umwelt,: wrong punctuation — each sentence (einerseits / andererseits) is separate; Umwelt ends with a full stop, not a comma.

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are in town and meet a German-speaking journalist who is interviewing young people about environmental issues.

bullets.prompt: Say what you think the biggest environmental problem is and why.
bullets.model_answer: Meiner Meinung nach ist der Klimawandel das größte Problem, weil die Temperaturen steigen und es mehr Überschwemmungen gibt.
bullets.note: Meiner Meinung nach (opinion phrase, fronted — triggers inversion: ist), weil + verb-final (steigen and gibt both at end of respective clauses)

bullets.prompt: Say what you personally do for the environment.
bullets.model_answer: Ich fahre mit dem Rad zur Schule, ich recycele Papier und Plastik, und ich benutze keine Plastiktüten.
bullets.note: mit dem Rad (dative after mit), recycele (ich-form — e added before personal ending), keine (kein negates noun)

bullets.prompt: Say what everyone should do, using modal verbs.
bullets.model_answer: Man sollte weniger Auto fahren und öffentliche Verkehrsmittel benutzen. Wir müssen auch Energie und Wasser sparen.
bullets.note: man sollte + infinitive at end (fahren), wir müssen + infinitive at end (sparen)

bullets.prompt: Give a balanced argument about renewable energy.
bullets.model_answer: Einerseits ist erneuerbare Energie gut für die Umwelt. Andererseits ist sie oft teuer und nicht überall verfügbar.
bullets.note: einerseits/andererseits (balanced argument structure), sie referring to die Energie (feminine pronoun)

gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a role play about the environment. This takes place in town — a semi-formal context. For each bullet, assess: (1) Did they communicate the required information? (2) Is the German grammatically accurate? Check: modal verbs (sollte, müssen) with infinitive at end, weil + verb-final, future tense if used (werden + infinitive at end), balanced argument connectives (einerseits/andererseits), pronoun agreement (sie for die Energie), noun capitalisation. Award marks out of 10 total. Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"Per-bullet feedback","improvement":"Key grammar point to revise"}

gold.question: Write 40-50 words in German about the environment. Include: one environmental problem, what you personally do to help, what everyone should do, and what will happen in the future if we do not act.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking extended writing about the environment. Mark on: Communication (did they address all four bullet points?), Range of language (modal verbs sollte/müssen + infinitive at end, werden + infinitive for future predictions, einerseits/andererseits or zwar...aber for balance, weil/wenn + verb-final), Accuracy (noun capitalisation, modal + infinitive placement — infinitive must be at clause end not adjacent to modal, future tense formation, kein vs nicht). Be encouraging and formative. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Wenn wir nichts tun, wird der Klimawandel schlimmer werden, und viele Tiere werden aussterben.
gold.correct_text: Wenn wir nichts tun, wird der Klimawandel schlimmer werden, und viele Tiere werden aussterben.
gold.translation: If we do nothing, climate change will get worse, and many animals will become extinct.

gold.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
gold.english: Admittedly recycling is important, but it is **not enough**. We **must not** destroy the environment.
sentence_parts: Zwar ist Recycling wichtig, aber es reicht nicht

gaps.correct_explain: aus is the separated prefix of ausreichen (to be sufficient / enough). Es reicht nicht aus = it is not enough. In a main clause the prefix moves to the end.

wrong.genug: genug (enough) can work in the phrase es ist nicht genug, but here the structure es reicht nicht aus (the separable verb) is the target.

gaps.correct_explain: dürfen ... nicht = must not (prohibition). Wir dürfen die Umwelt nicht zerstören = we must not destroy the environment.

wrong.müssen: müssen nicht means 'don't have to' (no obligation). For prohibition ('must not'), use dürfen nicht.
wrong.sollen: sollen nicht = are not supposed to (external instruction). For a strong prohibition, dürfen nicht is more appropriate.
